title: How Does a Microwave Oven Heat Food?
note: TEST FIXTURE ONLY: not fact-checked, not for upload. Used to check that a different video is NOT flagged as a duplicate.

sentences.text: Heat soup in a microwave and the bowl can stay cool while the soup boils.
How can an oven heat the food but not the air around it?
A microwave oven makes radio waves with a part called a magnetron.
The waves bounce around the metal box and pass into the food.
They are the same family of waves as radio and Wi-Fi, just at a chosen frequency.
Water molecules have a positive end and a negative end.
The changing electric field of the wave twists them back and forth billions of times a second.
All that jostling rubs neighbouring molecules and turns into heat.
The waves form a pattern of hot and cold spots inside the box.
That is why ovens have a turntable, to move food through the hot spots.
Frozen water heats poorly, so ice can stay frozen next to boiling patches.
Metal reflects the waves instead of absorbing them.
Sharp metal edges can gather charge and make sparks.
A microwave oven heats food by making its water molecules shake.
The plate stays cooler because it holds little water.
